descript.abstract: This dataset shows linear bikeways throughout Minnesota. Data is gathered through annual update requests of many public partners including County and Municipal contacts, Metropolitan Planning Organizations, Regional Development Commissions and the Minnesota DNR. Updates are occasionally provided by private partners including the MTB project and consulting agencies. Comments and corrections people submit on the Minnesota Bikeways Crowdsourcing App also inform the dataset. The data is vetted and maintained by the Geographic Information Mapping unit in the MnDOT Transportation System Management Office, and staff in the Transit and Active Transportation Office of MnDOT. The initial dataset was developed in partnership with the Minnesota Geospatial Advisory Council, and the Minnesota Geospatial Information Office.
descript.purpose: The purpose of this data set is to provide a single, commonly accepted set of attribute specifications (bikeway name, type, and length) for aggregating and mapping bikeways data in Minnesota. It will improve the ability to share data resources between parties by reducing incompatibilities when acquiring, processing, storing, and disseminating bikeways data. This data set will be useful to local, regional, and state governments for identifying network gaps within and between jurisdictions, easing data transfer between all levels of government and across partnering stakeholder organizations, and – in context with other feature classes / shapefiles – providing data critical for level of service, level of traffic stress and other network evaluations.

timeperd.current: Data will be reviewed and updated at least every other year in accordance with Minnesota State Statute 160.262.

lineage.procstep: All attributes in this feature class are derived from the Structure Inventory Management System (SIMS) where structures are added, managed and removed from inventory. The data is managed by the Bridge Inventory Management Unit (BIMU) located at the MnDOT Bridge Office. Most location fields remain static through the life of a structure, other fields will change and can be changed by the owner agency based on routine field inspections. All structures are aligned with the LRS route network, while not in the attribute table this information can be obtained through a request to the data contact in this metadata. The bridge and LRS integration data are quality checked automatically weekly and changes are made periodically throughout the inspection year when there are route number changes or route modifications (measure changes). MnDOT has regularly requested and collected bikeways data from local, regional and state partners since the 1990s for the creation of the Statewide Bicycle Maps. Since 2013, MnDOT has compiled, maintained, published, and distributed a map of bikeways every other year in compliance with Minnesota State Statute 160.262. Initially, updates were primarily submitted as hand drawn lines on paper or written explanations of bikeway features and placements. In the 2010s, the bikeways map was converted from paper to CADD which made sharing status and receiving updates easier. In 2018, the bikeways map was converted to GIS, and MnDOT's LRS team began supporting and maintaining bikeway information (including road shoulder surface type and widths). In 2021, the Bikeways Data Standard was developed in partnership with the MnGAC and MnGEO, and work began to convert all historically relevant data into the standard which improved mapping and management abilities. dataqual.complete: MnDOT requests annual updates from many public partners including County and Municipal contacts, Metropolitan Planning Organizations, Regional Development Commissions and the Minnesota DNR. Updates are occasionally provided by private partners including the MTB project and some consulting agencies. In addition, anyone at anytime can submit comments and corrections through the crowdsource reporter. All these data segments are vetted by MnDOT staff before they are added to the bikeways dataset.

horizpa.horizpar: This dataset is best suited for general reference. Data has been appended from multiple sources which have varying levels of accuracy. A portion of the data has been georeferenced and digitized using aerial photography. There is a continual effort to improve data quality and completeness. Each addition is a step toward the long-term goal of having a complete statewide bikeways layer for ongoing use by Minnesota's GIS community.

dataqual.logic: All features in this Bikeways dataset have been validated to assure they meet the Bikeways Data Standard attribute specifications and domains.

Feature geometry

This is intended to be a persistent unique identifier derived from a Globally Unique Identifier (GUID) for the segment. A GUID is a 36-character unique identifier generated using a standardized process to ensure a minimum probability of duplication.
Proper name of the bikeway or bikeway segment
Name of the overall bikeway system that may be comprised of multiple bikeways
Alternate bikeway name that is used when the bikeway is part of more than one route or has more than one use. Multiple bikeway names may be included in this field separated by a comma.

This field indicates the bicycling facility’s main function. It also describes whether the bicycling facility is located on-road (on the same grade as a parallel road) or off-road (on a different grade from a parallel road)

Whether the bikeway is part of a private system such as velodromes, summer mountain bike trails at private ski hills, and bikeways on company campuses
Owner of the land beneath the bikeway
Type of entity which owns the land beneath the bikeway
Name of the bikeway’s managing or administrative organization. This may be different from the landowner
Type of the bikeway’s managing or administrative organization
Current status of the bikeway. That is, if and how the bikeway is available to users
The predominant surface type users would expect to encounter on the bikeway

attr.attrdef: Year that the bikeway is programmed for construction or funding.
Year that the bikeway first opened for use.
Width of the bikeway segment in feet. May be approximated if there are frequent changes in width.
Whether the bikeway is open for seasonal or year-round use.
Permitted direction of travel on the bikeway.

Whether pavement marking exists along the bikeway. Pavement markings exist on bikeways to indicate the separation of the lanes for road users, assist the bicyclist by indicating assigned travel paths, indicate correct position for traffic signal actuation, and provide advance information for turning and crossing maneuvers.
Whether lighting exists along the bikeway segment.
Whether active transportation related signing (i.e., regulatory, warning, or wayfinding signs) exists along the bikeway segment.

Whether the bikeway is part of a separation system, as well as the type of separation. A separated bikeway can be an on-street bicycle lane that has physical separation from vehicles, such as bollards.
